title: Choose Redis caching vs database optimization
description: Decide whether to introduce Redis as a caching layer or invest in database indexing, query optimization, and read replicas for a read-heavy e-commerce product catalog.

data.text: Your product catalog page is timing out. Database CPU is pegged at 90 percent during traffic spikes. Your instinct is to add Redis. But your CTO wants to know whether a cache is treating a symptom or solving a root cause, and whether the operational complexity of cache invalidation is worth it.

terms.definition: The application checks the cache first; on miss, it queries the database and writes the result back.
The cache sits in front of the database and writes go to both cache and database simultaneously.
The process of removing or updating stale cache entries when underlying data changes.
Many concurrent cache misses causing a flood of identical database queries.
A database instance that replicates data from a primary to offload read traffic.

data.title: Cache invalidation is one of the two hard problems in CS
data.text: Phil Karlton famously said there are only two hard things in Computer Science: cache invalidation and naming things. A cache that returns stale data is worse than a slow database: users see outdated prices or inventory.

cards.title: Redis Cache-Aside
cards.description: Add Redis as an external caching tier to absorb read traffic.
pros: Orders of magnitude faster reads for hot keys
TTL provides a natural staleness ceiling
Useful for session state, feature flags, and rate limiting too
cons: Cache invalidation logic adds significant application complexity
Cold start thundering herd if Redis restarts
Another failure domain to monitor and operate
Stale reads until TTL expires or invalidation fires

cards.title: Database Optimization
cards.description: Index tuning, query optimization, and read replica promotion.
pros: Single source of truth, no consistency concerns
No new infrastructure or client libraries
Read replicas scale horizontally without application changes
PostgreSQL query planner can optimize dynamically
cons: Indexes add write latency and storage cost
Replica lag means reads can be stale
Requires deep knowledge of query plans and statistics
Scaling reads requires adding and managing replicas

data.title: C# cache-aside with Redis
data.content: Application-controlled caching with explicit invalidation on write.

data.title: Database: Composite index for catalog queries
data.content: If the bottleneck is a missing index, optimization is cheaper than a cache.
data.code:
-- Before: slow sequential scan on category + price
SELECT * FROM products
WHERE category_id = $1 AND price < $2
ORDER BY popularity DESC;

-- After: covering index avoids table access
CREATE INDEX idx_products_category_price_pop
ON products (category_id, price)
INCLUDE (name, image_url, popularity);

-- With partial index for in-stock items only:
CREATE INDEX idx_products_in_stock
ON products (category_id, popularity)
WHERE stock_count > 0;

items.text: Is the read pattern cacheable, or are writes invalidating entries too frequently?
Can query optimization and indexing resolve the issue without new infrastructure?
Does your team have Redis expertise for connection management and failover?
Are reads skewed toward a small set of hot products?
Can you tolerate serving slightly stale data?

data.caption: Adding a cache introduces a new failure domain
data.definition:
graph TD
    A[Client Request] --> B{Cache Hit?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Return cached value]
    B -->|No| D[Query Database]
    D --> E[Write to Cache]
    E --> F[Return value]
    G[Write Request] --> H[Update Database]
    H --> I[Invalidate Cache]
    I --> J{Invalidation Works?}
    J -->|Yes| K[Consistent]
    J -->|No| L[Stale Data]

data.title: Recommended approach: Optimize the database first, add Redis selectively
data.content: Add the missing composite index and a single read replica. Measure again. If p99 latency is still above target, add Redis only for the top 1 percent of hot products. Keep the cache small and the invalidation logic centralized.
data.code:
-- Step 1: Fix the index
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_products_optimized
ON products (category_id, popularity)
INCLUDE (name, price, image_url);

-- Step 2: Add read replica for reporting and catalog browsing
-- Application writes go to primary; reads route via connection pooler

-- Step 3: Redis for hot products only
-- Keys: product:hot:{id}
-- TTL: 60 seconds
-- Populated by background job, not lazy caching

data.title: Alternative for extreme scale
data.text: If hot products represent more than 30 percent of reads, consider a CDN or edge cache. Redis is best for application-level caching, not full-page caching at scale.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Optimize the database before adding infrastructure.
Cache invalidation complexity grows faster than cache value.
Use Redis for hot keys and short TTLs, not as a primary data store.
data.takeaway: The right cache is one you can delete without breaking correctness.
